# LCARdS

> LCARdS is a Star Trek LCARS-style card system for Home Assistant: custom Lovelace cards (button, elbow, slider, chart, data grid, select menu, layout card, alert overlay, MSD ship displays), a layout view and a shell dashboard strategy, configured in YAML, with themes, rules, data sources, animations, sounds and an alert mode.

These docs describe LCARdS 2026.10.0-dev.3. When writing LCARdS YAML, use only keys from the JSON Schemas below (do not invent keys), then check the result with the config checker. Every LCARdS card type is written as `type: custom:<name>` (for example `custom:lcards-button`).

## Machine-readable

- [Schema index](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/schema/index.json): one JSON Schema per card, view and strategy, the shared files each uses, and their sizes; load only the card you need
- [Full schema bundle](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/lcards-schema.json): every schema in one file (about 470 KB)
- [Built-in names](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/schema/registries.json): presets, components, animation and background presets, filters, sound assets, MSD backgrounds and theme tokens that values must match
- [Config checker](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/tools/lcards-validate.mjs): `node lcards-validate.mjs dashboard.yaml` checks a card, view or whole dashboard (Node 20+, one file)
- [All user docs in one file](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/llms-full.txt): getting started, configuration, cards and core as markdown
- [LCARdS skill](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/tools/lcards-skill.zip): instructions plus all of the above in one package (Agent Skills format: Claude Code, claude.ai and other compatible tools)
- [Claude Code marketplace](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/marketplace.json): the same skill as a Claude Code plugin (`/plugin marketplace add https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/marketplace.json`, then `/plugin install lcards@<marketplace name>`)
- [Getting AI help](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/ai-assistance.html): what to attach and a prompt template

## Getting started

- [Getting AI Help](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/ai-assistance.html): Get Claude, ChatGPT or another AI assistant to write LCARdS YAML that works: the LCARdS skill for Claude, what to give other assistants, and how to check the result.
- [Building a Dashboard](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/building-dashboards.html): How to compose an LCARS dashboard from LCARdS cards: which card for which job, laying out a screen on a layout view, and recipes for rules, data sources and alert mode.
- [Coming from CB-LCARS](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/cb-lcars-migration.html): LCARdS originates from, and supersedes, the CB-LCARS project.
- [Check Your Config](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/config-checker.html): Paste LCARdS YAML (a card, a view or a whole dashboard) and see every unknown option, misspelt name and invalid value, with its line and a link to the docs. Runs in your browser.
- [Dashboard Gallery](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/dashboard-gallery.html): Complete LCARdS dashboards to copy (bridge, engineering, environmental, security, alert mode, Picard-era operations and sciences screens, and six screens built from the design guide), with the...
- [Getting Help](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/getting-help.html): Something not working? Work through these in order: most problems are a config typo or a setup issue, and both are quick to rule out.
- [Installation](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/installation.html): Install LCARdS from HACS, add the integration (Home Assistant 2026.10 or newer) and set it up from the LCARdS Config Panel.
- [Designing LCARS Screens](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/lcars-design.html): Guidelines for making a Home Assistant dashboard look like LCARS: frames, colour roles from your theme, the Picard and classic TNG/DS9/Voyager looks, motion, and patterns built from LCARdS cards.
- [What is LCARdS?](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/what-is-lcards.html): What LCARdS is: LCARS-style cards, a layout view and a shell dashboard for Home Assistant, with themes, rules, data sources, animations, sounds and alert modes, and how the pieces fit together.

## Configuration

- [Configuration](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/): LCARdS configuration is managed through the LCARdS Config Panel, a dedicated sidebar entry in Home Assistant that serves as the central control hub for your installation. It provides access to...
- [Alert Mode Lab](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/alert-mode-lab.html): The Alert Mode Lab is a tab in the LCARdS Config Panel for customising the colour palette applied to each alert level. Changes can be previewed live before saving.
- [Using LCARdS with browser_mod](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/browser-mod.html): LCARdS and browsermod are complementary: LCARdS handles full-screen graphical alerts and theme transforms, browsermod handles popups, navigation, and device sensors. They work side-by-side without...
- [Connection Overlay](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/connectivity.html): Full-screen overlay shown whenever Home Assistant loses its WebSocket connection
- [HA Actions](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/ha-actions.html): Control LCARdS from automations, scripts, voice assistants, and Developer Tools
- [HA-LCARS Theme Lab](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/ha-lcars-theme-lab.html): Build your own HA-LCARS theme profile in the LCARdS panel's HA-LCARS Theme Lab: palettes for HA's five colour roles, LCARS chrome, state colours, a live preview, and YAML to add to HA-LCARS.
- [LCARdS Theme Profiles for HA-LCARS](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/ha-lcars-theme-profiles.html): HA-LCARS includes two themes made for LCARdS: LCARS Picard [LCARdS Red Accent] and LCARS Picard [LCARdS Blue Accent]. Pick one and Home Assistant's own screens, the HA-LCARS chrome and your LCARdS...
- [Persistent Helpers](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/persistent-helpers.html): LCARdS uses Home Assistant input helpers to store settings persistently: alert mode state, sound configuration, and HA-LCARS sizing values. They survive HA restarts and can be used in automations.
- [Sound Configuration](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/sounds.html): LCARS-style audio feedback for card interactions and HA UI events
- [Users & Devices](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/users-devices.html): The Users & Devices tab in the LCARdS Config Panel is the central place to view and manage the devices and users that have stored per-device or per-user setting overrides.

## Cards

- [The Fleet](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/): Every LCARdS card at a glance (button, elbow, slider, chart, data grid, select menu, layout card, alert overlay, MSD) with links to each card's reference.
- [Alert Overlay Card](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/alert-overlay/): The Alert Overlay card reacts to the inputselect.lcardsalertmode helper and displays a full-screen backdrop and content card whenever the system enters an alert state. It is a singleton...
- [Button Card](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/button/): The Button card covers everything from simple labels and toggle buttons to complex interactive components like D-pads and multi-segment SVG controls. Elbows are derived from the same base - most...
- [Button Playground](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/button/playground.html): Edit the YAML and the card redraws as you type. Pick a starting point (a lozenge toggle, state colours, a bar-label header or a sensor readout), then change the preset, label or colours.
- [Chart Card](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/chart/): Plots your Home Assistant sensors over time: lines, areas, columns, gauges, range bands, candlesticks and more. Charts pick up your LCARS theme colours and fonts automatically, so most charts need...
- [Chart Playground](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/chart/playground.html): Edit the YAML and the chart redraws as you type. Pick a starting point from the list, or paste a chart from your own dashboard.
- [Series & Time](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/chart/series.html): What each series plots, how much time the chart shows, and how to combine points, mix chart types and add Y axes. For where series data comes from (entity history, long-term statistics or an...
- [Styling](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/chart/styling.html): Charts use your theme's colours and fonts without any style at all, so everything on this page is optional. Colours accept every format in Colours: var(--lcars-), theme: tokens, hex and rgba.
- [Upgrading](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/chart/upgrading.html): Earlier versions of the chart card used a different layout for series (source, seriesnames, numbered series1 data sources, and so on). You don't need to change anything: older charts keep working...
- [Common Card Properties](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/common.html): LCARdS share a set of common top-level configuration properties regardless of card type. This page documents them alongside how sizing interacts with the HA grid system.
- [Data Grid Card](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/data-grid/): A grid of cells in the LCARS style. Use it two ways:
- [Data & Cells](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/data-grid/data.html): In data mode you write the grid row by row. Each row is a list of cells, and the card works out what each cell is.
- [Data Grid Playground](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/data-grid/playground.html): Edit the YAML and the grid redraws as you type. Pick a starting point from the list, or paste a grid from your own dashboard.
- [Styling & Animation](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/data-grid/styling.html): Every cell gets its style from up to six layers. Later layers win, key by key:
- [Upgrading](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/data-grid/upgrading.html): Earlier versions of the data grid used a few different keys: a second animation: block next to animations:, numeric grid sizes, top-level font settings, and cell styles kept in a separate list....
- [Elbow Card](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/elbow/): The Elbow card creates the iconic LCARS corner/cap shapes: the L-shaped coloured bars that frame sections of an LCARS interface. Extends the button card so it inherits text, actions, rules,...
- [Elbow Playground](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/elbow/playground.html): Edit the YAML and the card redraws as you type. Pick a starting point (a header or footer elbow, or the segmented style), then change the elbow type, bar sizes or colours.
- [Layout Card](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/layout-card/): The LCARdS Layout Card (custom:lcards-layout-card): a CSS Grid of cards inside one card, with the Layout Studio visual editor. Also the replacement for custom:layout-card.
- [Layout View](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/layout-view/): A custom dashboard view type with a built-in, in-view WYSIWYG CSS Grid editor: build a grid layout visually (drag to resize tracks, draw areas, drop cards into them) right on the dashboard, the...
- [Main Engineering](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/main-engineering.html): Main Engineering is a tab in every LCARdS card editor. It is a live window into the systems behind the card: its data sources, rules, theme tokens and templates, and where each of its values comes...
- [MSD Card](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/msd/): Master Systems Display: a zoomable SVG canvas on which you position any Home Assistant card as an overlay. Lines (routes) connect anchors across the canvas, and shapes (polylines, rectangles,...
- [Base SVG Filters Reference](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/msd/base-svg-filters.html): Visual filters for base SVG layer Apply opacity, blur, brightness, tint, and other effects to make overlays more prominent
- [Control Overlay](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/msd/control-overlay.html): Embeds any Home Assistant card (built-in or custom) at a fixed position on the MSD canvas. Supports all 9 attachment points for line connections.
- [Line Overlay](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/msd/line-overlay.html): Connects two overlays (controls, other lines' anchors, or shapes) with a routed SVG line. Supports automatic or manual routing, attachment side control, gap offsets, state-based color, and rich...
- [Manual Routing](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/msd/manual-routing.html): Manual routing allows you to explicitly define the path a line takes by specifying waypoints. The line will travel through each waypoint in the order they appear in the array.
- [MSD Quick Start](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/msd/quick-start.html): MSD (Master Systems Display) is the most involved card in LCARdS: it's less a single card and more a small canvas editor of its own. This is a quick UI-only walkthrough showing the buttons and...
- [Routing Concepts](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/msd/routing-concepts.html): MSD lines route themselves like cable raceways on a circuit board: they find their own way around obstacles, bundle together when they're heading the same direction, and avoid cutting across each...
- [Line Routing & Channels](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/msd/routing.html): MSD lines are routed like cable raceways on a circuit board: lines that travel in the same direction bundle together into evenly-spaced parallel lanes, branch apart where their destinations...
- [Shape Overlay](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/msd/shape-overlay.html): Freeform geometry on the MSD canvas: polylines (walls, connectors, custom paths), rectangles and circles (rooms, zones, highlights). Shares its full styling system with the Line Overlay: dashed...
- [Select Menu Card](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/select-menu/): Renders an inputselect or select entity as a grid of LCARS-styled option buttons. Tapping a button calls selectoption on the entity and the card updates immediately to reflect the new active option.
- [Select Menu Playground](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/select-menu/playground.html): Edit the YAML and the card redraws as you type. Pick a starting point (options from an inputselect, or custom labels), then change the preset or the grid.
- [Slider Card](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/slider-card/): Interactive sliders and read-only gauges for entities like lights, covers, fans, climate, and sensors. Four main visual styles: segmented pill bars, ruler gauges, shaped (clip-path fill) and the...
- [Slider Playground](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/slider-card/playground.html): Edit the YAML and the card redraws as you type. Pick a starting point (a brightness pill bar, a temperature gauge or a number level), then change the preset or the entity.

## Core features

- [Features](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/): What every LCARdS card can do (actions, colours, text, animations, sounds) and the shared services behind them (themes, rules, data sources, templates, alert mode).
- [Actions](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/actions.html): LCARdS cards support actions tapaction, holdaction, and doubletapaction. These follow the standard Home Assistant action model.
- [Alert Mode](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/alert-mode.html): Alert Mode gives LCARdS coordinated, dashboard-wide visual states that match the classic Star Trek red/yellow alert experience.
- [Entity Change Triggers](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/animations/entity-change-triggers.html): The onentitychange trigger fires an animation whenever a watched entity's state (or attribute) changes. This page covers the full set of options available for entity-based triggering.
- [Animation Preset Reference](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/animations/preset-reference.html): All built-in animation presets, their parameters, and defaults. Pass preset-specific parameters via the params block in your animation config.
- [Rule-based Animations](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/animations/rule-based-animations.html): The Rules Engine can trigger animations across any number of cards simultaneously when conditions are met. This is more powerful than per-card onentitychange animations when you need to coordinate...
- [Card Animations](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/animations.html): LCARdS cards support anime.js-powered animations triggered by user interactions or entity state changes. Each card can have multiple animations with different triggers.
- [Borg Assimilation](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/borg.html): The Borg Assimilation mode uses LCARdS core systems to tranform the entire dashboard interface into a Borg-assimilated state:
- [Colours](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/colours.html): LCARdS accepts several colour formats wherever a colour value is expected. You can use static values (hex, CSS variables, theme tokens), state-based maps that change automatically with entity...
- [Data Sources](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/datasources/): Data Sources give cards access to entity history, real-time updates, and processed values, beyond the plain current state that HA cards normally see.
- [Processor Reference](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/datasources/processor-reference.html): Complete reference for all 12 DataSource processor types.
- [Background Animation Preset Reference](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/effects/background-animations/preset-reference.html): All built-in background animation presets with full configuration options and examples. Pass preset-specific parameters via the config block in each effect entry.
- [Background Animations](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/effects/background-animations.html): Animated canvas-based backgrounds for LCARdS cards
- [Filters](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/effects/filters.html): LCARdS cards support stackable CSS and SVG visual filters applied directly to the card's rendered output. Combine multiple filters in any order to create blur, glow, colour shift, grain, or...
- [Screen Effects](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/effects/screen-effects.html): Full-screen visual effects that sit above all HA and LCARdS UI
- [Presets](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/presets.html): Presets are named collections of style properties. Applying a preset to a card sets its shape, colours, typography, border, and state appearances in one step, instead of writing all those...
- [Rules Engine](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/rules/): Rules let you apply style changes to groups of cards based on entity state, without touching each card individually. A single rule can update dozens of overlays at once.
- [Rule Conditions](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/rules/conditions.html): The when block of a rule evaluates to true or false. When it matches, the rule's apply block fires. When it stops matching, the patch is removed.
- [Card Sounds](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/sounds.html): LCARdS cards play audio feedback automatically for interactions: taps, holds, hover, slider drags, and toggle state changes. No config is needed to get the default behaviour; sounds follow the...
- [Card Styles](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/styles.html): The style: block controls the visual appearance of a card: background colours, borders, and dimensions. Style values layer on top of a preset and can be further overridden at runtime by the Rules...
- [Templates](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/templates/): LCARdS cards support dynamic content through four template syntaxes. You can mix them freely in most string values.
- [Text Fields](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/text-fields.html): Most LCARdS cards support a text object that lets you place any number of labelled text fields anywhere on the card. Fields inherit from a shared default block so you only need to set what differs...
- [Themes](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/core/themes/): To complement the HA-LCARS system theme - LCARdS adds a token-based theme system for its cards. Instead of hardcoding colours and other default settings, we can reference named tokens that the...

- [Asset Manager](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/architecture/subsystems/asset-manager.html): window.lcards.core.assetManager: Named asset loading, URL registry, and caching.
- [Component Manager](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/architecture/subsystems/component-manager.html): window.lcards.core.componentManager: Registry of SVG component definitions for button component mode.

- [Building a Pack](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/development/building-a-pack.html): A pack is a self-contained bundle of themed assets that a third party (or you) can distribute to extend LCARdS. A single pack can contribute any combination of style presets, components, themes,...
- [Building a Card Editor](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/development/building-an-editor.html): LCARdS ships a visual editor for every built-in card. This guide shows how to add one to your own card.
- [Colour Resolution: Developer Guide](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/development/colour-resolution.html): Every LCARdS colour goes through one grammar and one resolver. This page says which call to use in which context, so a colour that works in one card works in all of them.
- [Building a Custom Card](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/development/custom-card.html): This guide walks through creating a new LCARdS card from scratch, from the class skeleton through registration in Home Assistant.
- [Debug API](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/development/debug-api.html): Browser console tools for LCARdS development, accessed via window.lcards.debug.
- [HA CSS Variable Reference](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/development/ha-css-vars.html): HA 2026.6+ required. All variables documented here are available from HA 2026.6 onwards. Source files are in the HA frontend repository.
- [Helpers API - Developer Guide](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/development/helpers-api.html): This guide explains the architecture and usage of the LCARdS helper management system for developers extending or maintaining the codebase.
- [Type Checking: Developer Guide](https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/development/typescript.html): LCARdS is written in plain JavaScript, and TypeScript checks it. Nothing is compiled: tsc reads the .js files and their JSDoc comments, reports mistakes and writes no output. The Vite build...
